The failing test `testRead7ZipMultiVolumeArchiveForStream` is testing the functionality of reading a multi-volume ZIP archive using `ZipArchiveInputStream` from `org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.zip`. The test verifies that when a truncated archive is encountered, an exception is thrown with the message "Truncated ZIP file".

The current bug report states that `ZipArchiveInputStream.read()` method does not report the end of a truncated archive properly. It mentions that when a Zip archive is truncated, the `read()` method will return 0 bytes read instead of -1 (end of stream) or throwing an exception.

By looking at the source code of `org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.zip.ZipArchiveInputStream.read(byte[], int, int)`, we can see that the method checks if the current entry is finished and returns -1 if so. However, it doesn't seem to have specific handling for detecting a truncated archive and signaling an end of stream condition.

To fix the issue, the `ZipArchiveInputStream.read()` method needs to include additional logic to detect a truncated archive and properly signal an end of stream condition or throw an exception. This can help the calling code to handle truncated archives more effectively.

The method that needs to be fixed:
```java
org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.zip.ZipArchiveInputStream.read(byte[], int, int)
```

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
